headline: A 2018 law requires federal agencies that build or redesign public websites to make them work on smartphones and tablets.
what_it_does: When a federal agency creates or redesigns a website meant for the public, the site must be mobile friendly. Mobile friendly means it can be navigated, viewed, and accessed on a smartphone, tablet, or similar device. The Office of Management and Budget must also report on how well agencies follow this rule.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that create or redesign public websites
who_it_affects.how: They must make new or redesigned public-facing websites work well on mobile devices.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the public who use federal websites
who_it_affects.how: People visiting covered federal sites on phones or tablets should be able to navigate and access them on those devices.
It must report on whether agencies are complying with the mobile-friendly requirement.
